answer: Picture a wharf where every newcomer must earn a berth through liquid reputation delegation: veterans publicly lend a slice of their own standing, revocable at any time, and the ledger records each loan. Delegations traced to one tight cluster count as a single voice, so a farm cannot multiply itself by lending to its own clones across the tundra of lookalike accounts. Each loan expires each season unless renewed. If a backed newcomer cheats, every delegator loses standing too, making each loan a real risk. Like a comet, trust arrives bright but brief unless renewed by honest work.
